extra.message: POST /app/usersearch concatenates req.body.login into a SQL query executed by sequelize.query(). An authenticated attacker can inject SQL, including UNION queries that extract user password hashes.

cwe: CWE-89: SQL Injection

extra.message: POST /app/ping concatenates req.body.address into a shell command passed to child_process.exec(). Shell metacharacters allow any authenticated user to execute arbitrary operating-system commands with the application's privileges.

cwe: CWE-78: OS Command Injection

extra.message: POST /app/bulkproductslegacy passes attacker-controlled uploaded bytes directly to node-serialize.unserialize(). Serialized function expressions can execute during deserialization, before products.forEach(), allowing authenticated remote code execution.

cwe: CWE-502: Deserialization of Untrusted Data

extra.message: POST /app/bulkproducts parses uploaded XML with noent:true, enabling external entity substitution. An authenticated attacker can reference local files in product fields; the expanded contents are saved and exposed through /app/products. The client-supplied MIME type does not prevent this.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: Unauthenticated POST /resetpw authorizes password changes using token == md5(login). Anyone knowing a username can calculate its token and replace the account password. Tokens require no reset request, never expire, and remain reusable.

cwe: CWE-640: Weak Password Recovery Mechanism for Forgotten Password

extra.message: POST /app/useredit selects the account using req.body.id without comparing it with req.user.id or checking privileges. Any authenticated user can submit another account's ID and overwrite its password, email, and name, taking over that account.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: /app/admin/usersapi and /app/admin/users require authentication but never require the admin role. The role check only hides dashboard content in the browser. Any registered user can directly request the administrative user listing.

cwe: CWE-862: Missing Authorization

extra.message: listUsersAPI fetches and serializes complete User records without an attribute allowlist. The model includes password, so /app/admin/usersapi exposes every user's bcrypt hash alongside account details, enabling offline password guessing.

cwe: CWE-201: Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Sent Data

extra.message: POST /app/products assigns req.body.name to output.searchTerm, which this template renders with the unescaped EJS tag <%- output.searchTerm %>. Submitted HTML and event handlers execute in the application's origin.

cwe: CWE-79: Cross-site Scripting

extra.message: Product name, code, tags, and description are rendered with unescaped EJS tags. Authenticated users control these persisted fields through /app/modifyproduct and bulk imports, allowing stored scripts to execute when other users view or search products.

cwe: CWE-79: Cross-site Scripting

extra.message: The user listing assigns API-provided names and emails directly to innerHTML. Attackers can persist HTML event handlers in these fields during registration or profile updates, causing script execution when another user opens /app/admin/users.

cwe: CWE-79: Cross-site Scripting

extra.message: Product and profile updates accept ordinary form submissions authenticated solely by the session cookie. No CSRF token or Origin/Referer validation is implemented. An attacker-controlled page can submit changes, including a new password, when the victim's browser sends the session cookie.

cwe: CWE-352: Cross-Site Request Forgery

extra.message: Express sessions use the public, hardcoded signing secret 'keyboard cat'. Anyone can calculate valid cookie signatures for known session identifiers. Exploiting an authenticated session still requires a valid server-side session identifier.

cwe: CWE-321: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key

extra.message: The session cookie explicitly sets secure:false. Browsers can transmit the authentication cookie over unencrypted HTTP, allowing a network attacker to capture and replay it to hijack the session.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: Unauthenticated POST /forgotpw redirects existing usernames to /login with a success message, while nonexistent usernames receive an explicit error and /forgotpw redirect. These distinguishable responses allow account enumeration.

cwe: CWE-204: Observable Response Discrepancy

extra.message: Global express-fileupload middleware buffers multipart uploads without configured file-size, file-count, or aggregate limits. It runs before authentication, so unauthenticated clients can send oversized uploads to exhaust application memory.

cwe: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

extra.message: POST /app/calc synchronously evaluates arbitrary mathematical expressions without operation restrictions or resource limits. A short expression requesting an enormous matrix, such as zeros(1000000000), can exhaust memory or block the shared Node.js event loop.

cwe: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

extra.message: Malformed calculator expressions throw synchronously without application error handling. When NODE_ENV is unset, Express's default development error response exposes stack traces and internal filesystem paths. The supplied startup configuration does not set production mode.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: Both Sequelize constructors retain default SQL logging. User creation and password/profile updates generate queries containing bcrypt hashes and personal information, exposing these values through application console logs.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: POST /login performs password verification on every request without account lockout, attempt tracking, or rate-limiting middleware. Remote clients can make unrestricted password guesses against existing accounts.

cwe: CWE-307: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts

extra.message: Session deserialization authenticates solely by stored user ID. Password reset and profile-password changes update the password without revoking sessions or changing a session version. cwe: CWE-613: Insufficient Session Expiration

extra.message: Registration checks only that passwords are nonempty and match their confirmation. A one-character password is accepted; password-reset and profile-update handlers likewise enforce no minimum strength. Accounts can therefore use trivially guessable passwords.

cwe: CWE-521: Weak Password Requirements
